Recall the following:

- a function $f(x)$ is *even* if $f(-x)=f(x)$

- a function $f(x)$ is *odd* if $f(-x)=-f(x)$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin, so we have

$$
{\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

Notice that $f(x)=({2}^{x}-\frac{1}{{2}^{x}})$ is an odd function. Indeed, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =({2}^{(-x)}-\frac{1}{{2}^{(-x)}}) \\  & =({(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}-\frac{1}{(1/2)^{x}}) \\  & =(\frac{1}{{2}^{x}}-{2}^{x}) \\  & =-({2}^{x}-\frac{1}{{2}^{x}}) \\  & =-f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

So, because $f(x)=({2}^{x}-\frac{1}{{2}^{x}})$ is an odd function, we have

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{2}({2}^{x}-\frac{1}{{2}^{x}})\,\text{d}x=0.
$$
